name: OpenVLA
summary: OpenVLA fine-tunes a Prismatic VLM (Llama 2 7B with a fused DINOv2 + SigLIP visual encoder) on 970k Open X-Embodiment episodes, predicting discretized action tokens. It outperformed RT-2-X (55B) by 16.5% absolute across 29 tasks while being far smaller, and the authors showed LoRA fine-tuning plus 4-bit quantization brings adaptation within reach of a single A100, or an RTX 4090 for inference.
innovation: Fusing DINOv2 (spatial/geometric) with SigLIP (semantic) features, measurably better for control than either alone.
Parameter-efficient LoRA adaptation of a large VLA to new robots at roughly 1% of full-tuning compute.
Released everything: weights, data mixture, fine-tuning scripts, evaluation harness.
matters: Became the default open VLA baseline; a large share of subsequent papers are OpenVLA variants.
Proved open reproductions can exceed closed frontier robot models.
limits: Single-image, single-arm, ~5 Hz autoregressive decoding, too slow for dynamic or bimanual work.
Action discretization caps precision on fine-grained motion.
lineage: An open re-derivation of RT-2's recipe on Open X-Embodiment data with a Llama-2 backbone.
